issues.detail: The Hebrew phrase 'אֲשֶׁר אֵין לָהֶם מְאוּמָה' means 'who had nothing' (i.e., the poorest of the people, those without possessions). The Chinese renders it as '一無過犯' (without any offense/guilt), which changes the meaning from 'having nothing' to 'having no fault/transgression.' This is a substantive mistranslation of the Hebrew.
